structure_text: A method is provided for generating an image from a medical device comprising an imaging system, an imaging device comprising a first and second section of the device, and an imaging device comprising a proximal portion of the device. In addition, the imaging device may be calibrated according to the orientation of the device. The imaging device comprises a plurality of instruments that are aligned at one end of the device with respect to a body surface, and a polarity modulator is applied to the instrument to determine the position of the instrument relative to the body surface.
llm_full: Systems and methods for multi-source image-guided calibration of medical instruments are disclosed. A plurality of imaging instruments, each associated with a respective coordinate frame and access path to an anatomical site, are configured to concurrently acquire image data of the site and one or more interventional instruments. A processing unit is configured to determine differences between coordinate frames of the multiple imaging sources and the interventional instruments, and to compute a unified control frame of reference based on the reconciled multi-source image data. The unified control frame is used to update instrument guidance, registration, and navigation parameters in real time to improve accuracy of image-guided interventions.
llm_title: A system and method are provided for image-guided control and calibration of medical instruments utilizing multi-source imaging data. The method includes acquiring patient-specific images from multiple modalities, registering the images to a common reference frame, and generating a composite guidance map. A medical instrument having a controllable actuation scheme is calibrated in real time based on the composite guidance map, with control parameters dynamically adjusted according to detected instrument position, tissue characteristics, and procedural stage. The system thereby enhances precision, safety, and repeatability of surgical interventions by tightly integrating calibrated instrument control with multi-source imaging feedback.

structure_text: A surgical imaging system comprises a device that is actuated by a first and second axis to determine the position of an instrument relative to a focal point. The instrument is synchronized with a detector at one end of the device, and a detector at the other end of the device is synchronized with a detector at the other end of the device. A signal transmission method comprising an array of optically modulated light sources may be employed to control the output of an optically modulated light source from a detector at one end of the device.
llm_full: A system and method are provided for multi-instrument medical navigation in which a plurality of scanning instruments access a common anatomical site via different access paths and share a coordinated imaging and control infrastructure. Each scanning instrument includes an imaging component configured to emit and/or receive light in distinct wavebands or modulation patterns to reduce crosstalk, while shared light sources, detectors, controllers, and processors generate multiplexed image data. A difference between respective coordinate frames associated with the instruments is determined based on the multiplexed image data, and a control frame of reference associated with at least one instrument is updated in response to the determined difference. The system enables simultaneous or time-multiplexed visualization and calibration of multiple instruments within a common anatomical site using a cost-efficient, shared imaging platform.
llm_title: A system and method are provided for calibrated control of multi-modal medical imaging instruments while eliminating illumination crosstalk between multiple imaging devices. A control scheme calibration unit determines device-specific response characteristics and control parameters for each imaging modality, including illumination intensity, timing, and wavelength profiles. A coordinated controller synchronizes and dynamically adjusts the operating states of the imaging devices based on the calibration data to minimize interference and optimize image quality. The system thereby enables accurate, co-registered medical imaging from multiple sources with reduced artifacts and improved diagnostic reliability.

structure_text: A system of the present invention provides a method for controlling and manipulating a surgical device. The system includes a motion sensor and a control mechanism for detecting and manipulating the motion of a surgical device. The control mechanism emits a resonant energy generated by the first and second components of the control mechanism. The resonant energy generated by the first and second components of the control mechanism is transmitted to a user at a fixed location. The resonant energy generated by the third component is transmitted to a user at a fixed location to be viewed.
llm_full: A system and method are provided for robotically assisted surgical bone removal using calibrated multi-instrument navigation. A first surgical instrument comprising a reciprocating bone-removal tool is controlled by a multi-axis robotic manipulator, and a second instrument comprising an imaging component accesses the same anatomical site via a different path. Image data from the second instrument is used to determine a difference between a first coordinate frame associated with the robotic bone-removal tool and a second coordinate frame associated with the imaging instrument. A control frame of reference for the robotic manipulator is updated based at least in part on the difference, thereby enabling precise, remotely controllable removal of hard tissue while avoiding soft tissue.
llm_title: A system and method are provided for calibrating a robotic surgical system using a control scheme calibration framework adapted for medical instruments. The system comprises one or more robotic arms, surgical tools, and sensors configured to acquire real-time instrument position, force, and orientation data during a calibration procedure. A processor executes control algorithms that compare sensed parameters to target calibration profiles and automatically adjusts control gains, motion scaling, and tool alignment to optimize accuracy and responsiveness. The calibrated control scheme enables improved precision, safety, and repeatability of robot-assisted surgical interventions.

structure_text: A surgical instrument system comprises a robotically actuated endoscope capable of manipulating a portion of a patient's body cavity. The robotically actuated endoscope is positioned proximal to the surgical instrument, and a guiding device is positioned proximal to the surgical instrument. The method of the invention includes a first-line technique for removing a portion of a patient's body cavity from a surgical instrument, and a second-line technique for insertion of a surgical instrument through a longitudinal slit.
llm_full: Systems and methods are provided for coordinated robotic surgical procedures that integrate endoscopically-assisted percutaneous access with multi-arm platform control. A first robotic arm manipulates an endoscopic instrument having an onboard position sensor introduced through a natural orifice to define a target location within a treatment region. A second robotic arm percutaneously guides a therapeutic instrument toward the target location based on real-time positional data from the first instrument and platform pose adjustments. A control circuit synchronizes movements of the robotic arms and compensates for changes in surgical platform position to maintain spatial registration and enable cooperative execution of diagnostic and interventional tasks.
llm_title: A surgical robotic system configured to perform concomitant endoscopic and percutaneous procedures using multiple cooperative robotic arms is disclosed. A first robotic arm manipulates an endoscope within a patient body cavity, while one or more additional robotic arms cooperatively position and actuate percutaneous instruments introduced through the patient’s skin. A cooperative control module coordinates motion, force, and instrument trajectories across the arms to maintain stable tool-to-endoscope relationships and shared target alignment. Methods are provided for synchronized path planning, collision avoidance, and dynamic adjustment of tool poses based on intraoperative imaging and sensor feedback.

structure_text: 1 A method for manipulating surgical instruments comprises a catheter-shaped endoscope and a catheter-shaped guide device. The catheter-shaped guide device generates an image of the catheter-shaped guide device. The catheter-shaped guide device generates an image of the catheter-shaped guide device. In addition, the method is able to determine a relative position of the catheter-shaped guide device within a patient's body cavity without the need for a radial emission system. In addition, the method is able to identify a point of obstruction within a patient's body cavity.
llm_full: A system and method for robotically-assisted percutaneous intervention are provided in which an endoscopically delivered instrument and a percutaneously delivered instrument are jointly localized using multi-sensor magnetic field tracking. A plurality of distinguishable magnetic fields are generated, and multiple sensors disposed near the distal ends of both instruments produce signals that are processed to determine six-degree-of-freedom pose for each instrument in a common reference frame. A target location is defined within a treatment region based on the endoscopic instrument pose, and the robotically-actuated percutaneous instrument is automatically guided toward and maintained at the target using the combined tracking data. The system can provide real-time visualization, collision avoidance, and coordinated control of both instruments during minimally invasive procedures.
llm_title: A prospective invention comprises an integrated robotic medical platform configured to perform concomitant endoscopic and percutaneous procedures while providing real-time diagnostic imaging and treatment capabilities. The system includes a coordinated robotic manipulator array operatively coupled to endoscopic instruments and percutaneous access tools, and further interfaces with multimodal imaging subsystems for intraoperative visualization and guidance. Diagnostic algorithms process imaging and sensor data to characterize tissue and pathology, and automatically adjust robotic tool trajectories and treatment parameters. Methods are provided for planning, executing, and updating combined diagnostic, interventional, and imaging workflows during a single, continuous minimally invasive procedure.

structure_text: A surgical tool system comprises a surgical instrument capable of manipulating an endoscope to perform a surgical procedure at a location proximal to the endoscope. A surgical instrument comprises a first-axis rotational motor coupled to a cutting tool. A surgical instrument comprises a laser-guided image transmission device. The laser-guided image transmission device is coupled to a cutting tool. A method for determining the position of a surgical instrument is also provided, and a method for determining the position of a surgical instrument is also provided, and a method for.
llm_full: A system and method are provided for managing and tracking usage of robotic surgical instruments during endoscopically-assisted percutaneous medical procedures. The method includes inserting a first medical instrument having an elongated shaft, a first position sensor, and at least one usage sensor into a treatment region of a patient through a natural orifice, and determining a first position of the first medical instrument within the treatment region. A second medical instrument is percutaneously guided toward a defined target location while images of the instruments are captured, a type of each robotic surgical instrument is identified based on the images, and a degree of usage of each instrument is determined from data acquired by the usage sensors. A stage in a life cycle of each instrument is then determined based on the identified instrument type and the determined degree of usage, and this life-cycle information is integrated into a robotically-enabled medical system to manage instrument selection, replacement, and procedural workflow.
llm_title: A prospective invention relates to integrated robotic surgical systems and methods configured to coordinate concomitant endoscopic and percutaneous procedures while dynamically tracking instrument usage. The system includes multiple robotic arms manipulable for endoscopic access and percutaneous access, a control console, and a data acquisition module that records tool identification, deployment sequence, contact events, and cumulative usage metrics for each surgical instrument. A processor executes control algorithms to synchronize multi-port access, optimize tool trajectories, and adjust operating parameters based on real-time usage data and predefined safety thresholds. The invention further provides methods for generating procedure logs, predictive maintenance schedules, and automated alerts when instruments exceed recommended use profiles during combined minimally invasive interventions.

structure_text: A system comprises a device for manipulating and tagging surgical instruments. The system includes a method for determining the position of a surgical instrument at a particular location. The method includes a first-arm motion detector coupled to one of the first-arm motion detectors. The method includes a set of control circuits that are electrically connected to at least one end of the system. In addition, a plurality of data input and output channels are provided to the system for generating and tagging a biometric image of the system.
llm_full: Systems and methods are provided for coordinated control of multiple robotic medical tools based on real-time fiducial identification and tracking. A robotic camera and one or more robotic tools are inserted through separate patient ports, with each tool and relevant anatomical structures bearing fiducial markers automatically detected and tracked in the camera image. Tool kinematics and fiducial tracking data are fused to maintain remote centers of motion and to automatically adjust tool and camera poses so that instruments and target anatomy remain within the field of view. In various modes, a single controller commands coordinated motion of tools relative to tracked fiducials, or separate controllers independently manipulate the camera and tools while the system autonomously maintains spatial relationships constrained by the fiducial positions.
llm_title: A system and method are provided for coordinating movements of multiple robotic surgical tools using real-time fiducial identification and tracking. The system includes a plurality of robotic instrument arms, each configured to manipulate a surgical tool, and an imaging subsystem configured to detect and track fiducial markers associated with anatomical structures, instruments, and/or reference frames. A control unit computes the spatial relationships between the fiducial markers and the robotic tools and generates coordinated motion commands that maintain desired tool-to-target geometries, collision avoidance, and constrained trajectories. In some embodiments, the system dynamically updates tool paths in response to intraoperative movement of tissue or instruments, thereby enabling precise, cooperative robotic maneuvers during minimally invasive surgical procedures.

structure_text: A medical robotic device of the invention comprises a coupling system to provide a method for manipulating a body cavity during a surgical procedure. The device is positioned within the body cavity to provide a recognizable image to the user. The device is positioned in the body cavity to provide a recognizable image to the user. The invention also provides a method for inserting an endoscope into a patient, wherein the endoscope is operated on by a centrally operated device, wherein the endoscope is operated on by a centrally controlled device.
llm_full: A robotic interventional medical system is provided for performing image-guided procedures within body cavities while coordinating multiple robotic tools and maintaining remote centers of motion. A multi-degree-of-freedom intracavitary device introduces and steers one or more medical instruments, such as needles, toward user-selected target points under real-time guidance from a medical imager. A robotic camera and additional treatment tools are controlled in coordinated modes so that the instruments remain within the camera’s field of view and comply with remote center-of-motion constraints at separate access ports or cavity entry points. Networked controllers process image data and user inputs to automatically synchronize tool trajectories, imaging viewpoints, and needle steering for precise, minimally invasive interventions performed locally or remotely.
llm_title: A system and method are provided for coordinated robotic insertion and manipulation of a medical device within a patient’s body during a medical imaging procedure. A plurality of robotic tools are controlled in a coordinated manner to position, guide, and actuate an interventional device in real time based on image-derived feedback. The system includes a controller configured to synchronize multi-axis robotic movements with imaging acquisition parameters to maintain optimal device orientation, trajectory, and visibility. Related apparatus, software, and workflows are disclosed for improving procedural accuracy, reducing manual intervention, and enhancing safety in image-guided interventions.

structure_text: A system of the invention includes a method for manipulating a surgical instrument, a device comprising at least one robotic actuator coupled to said actuator, and a device comprising a first-order camera coupled to said actuator. A method for obtaining and analyzing a patient's body position relative to said surgical instrument is provided. A method for transmitting and analyzing a patient's body position relative to said surgical instrument is provided. One or more embodiments of said embodiments may be configured to provide an electrical power source within said device.
llm_full: A robotic surgical system is provided in which coordinated movements of multiple robotic tools and an imaging device are adaptively controlled based on a detected procedural context. The system maintains remote centers of motion while automatically adjusting tool trajectories and camera pose in response to image-based identification of instruments, procedural phase, and region of interest. A first controller enables user-directed motion of a primary tool or camera, while secondary tools and imaging modalities are autonomously reconfigured to remain within the field of view and to match context-specific configuration parameters. In some embodiments, images from one modality and detected surgical phase trigger automatic switching or reconfiguration of other imaging modalities and tool coordination modes.
llm_title: A system and method are provided for performing coordinated, context-aware robotic interventions. A plurality of robotic tools are controlled via a coordination module that dynamically orchestrates multi-instrument movements based on a real-time surgical context model. The context model fuses sensor data, imaging, and procedural workflows to infer the current surgical phase, anatomical structures, and risk zones. Based on the inferred context, the system autonomously adjusts tool trajectories, interaction forces, and inter-tool timing to enhance safety, precision, and efficiency during the procedure.

structure_text: A method for actuating a surgical manipulating device includes a virtual user interface and a computer-based control system. The virtual user interface provides haptic feedback to a surgical manipulating device. The virtual user interface provides a method for actuating a surgical manipulating device at a predetermined position relative to a haptic force source. The device may be equipped with a receptacle to store a haptic force source, which is used to determine the shape of a surgical instrument. The device may be equipped with a three-dimensional shape.
llm_full: A surgical robotic system comprises an elongated guide section with a distal end member supporting a surgical tool, the attitude of the distal end member being adjusted by an internal attitude operation member driven by a controllable drive source. A non-contact attitude detection device detects the orientation of the distal end member relative to the guide section, and a control unit corrects attitude command values based on the detected attitude to compensate for variations in distal end straightness. The system further defines a virtual haptic interaction point associated with the surgical tool and establishes one or more virtual entry boundaries in the surgical field. A processing circuit activates haptic objects that constrain motion of the virtual haptic interaction point once a boundary is crossed, thereby providing virtual constraints on tool movement while maintaining accurate, automatically corrected distal end attitude control.
llm_title: A system and method are provided for remotely actuating and haptically controlling a surgical tool during minimally invasive or robotic procedures. The system includes a remotely operated actuator configured to translate operator input signals into precise mechanical motion of one or more surgical end-effectors. A haptic interface generates force, vibration, and/or tactile feedback to the operator based on real-time sensor data from the surgical site and actuator state, enabling intuitive bidirectional interaction. The integrated control architecture coordinates motion control and haptic feedback to enhance precision, safety, and situational awareness in teleoperated surgery.

structure_text: One of the methods of the present invention includes a virtual surgical tool system for manipulating anatomical data generated by a computer and displaying it to a user during a surgical procedure. The system is configured to detect anatomical changes in a patient during a surgical procedure. A user interface is configured to provide feedback to a surgeon on the anatomical position of a surgical implant. The anatomical position of a surgical implant can be correlated with the anatomical position of a surgical instrument, based on a combination of physical and electro-mechanical parameters.
llm_full: A computer-assisted surgical system integrates patient-matched instrumentation and haptic-constrained tool guidance for performing procedures on patient-specific anatomy. A three-dimensional model of the patient’s anatomy is generated and used to determine implant orientation, position, and the design of patient-matched guides that define one or more virtual entry boundaries. A surgical tool associated with a virtual haptic interaction point is registered to the patient-matched instrumentation, and a processing circuit activates haptic objects that constrain movement of the tool when the virtual haptic interaction point approaches or crosses the virtual entry boundaries. The system thereby provides patient-specific, haptically enforced guidance for accurate tool positioning and implant placement during surgery.
llm_title: A prospective system provides computer-assisted surgical procedures with integrated haptic feedback for enhanced precision and safety. The system includes a processor configured to generate a patient-specific surgical plan from preoperative imaging data and to register the plan to the patient anatomy in real time. A haptically controlled surgical tool is operatively coupled to the processor and is constrained by virtual boundaries corresponding to the planned resection or implant site, providing force feedback and guidance to the surgeon. The system may further adapt the haptic constraints based on intraoperative sensing, thereby dynamically updating the surgical plan and tool guidance during the procedure.

structure_text: A bi-sectional endoscopy device of the present invention comprises an implantable catheter that is able to be inserted into a body cavity for the purpose of generating an image of the surrounding tissue. The implantable catheter is anchored to the endoscope by means of a flexible suture. In addition, the implantable catheter is equipped with a magnetically activated ligand, a receptacle, and a protruding membrane. The ligand is positioned at the surface of the implantable catheter to facilitate insertion and dissection.
llm_full: A system and method for image-guided deployment of an implantable magnetic anastomosis device using fused endoscopic and laparoscopic ultrasound imaging is disclosed. An image fusion workstation generates a real-time composite view of an endoscopic image and an ultrasound image of a target anatomical region, and tracks a deliverable, self-assembling magnetic anastomosis device as it is advanced in a linear configuration through a minimally-invasive access route. The fused image space is used to determine optimal device positioning, tissue capture geometry, and polygonal self-assembly of the magnetic exoskeleton around circumscribed tissue. The system further enables monitoring of tissue apposition, necrosis, and perforation at the anastomosis site via the fused imaging modalities to guide intraoperative decisions and post-placement assessment.
llm_title: A system and method are provided for image-guided deployment of a self-assembling magnetic anastomosis device within a body lumen using fused endoscopic and ultrasound imaging. Endoscopic images are registered and fused in real time with intraluminal or external ultrasound images to generate a composite visualization of tissue structures and target sites for anastomosis. The fused image data are used to navigate and position at least two magnetic components of an anastomosis device having an exoskeleton so that they self-assemble across opposing tissue walls. The system may further include algorithms for automatic alignment, depth estimation, and verification of anastomosis formation based on multimodal image feedback.

structure_text: An endoscopic surgical tool comprises a robot-operated manipulator arm with a coupling mechanism that allows the manipulator arm to move relative to a surgical instrument. The coupling mechanism allows the manipulator arm to be flexibly accessed by a surgical instrument. A drive shaft is attached to the manipulator arm. The assembly includes a handle for controlling the movement of a surgical instrument, and a first-in, first-out, and second-in, middle-in, and third-in device for removing tissue from a surgical instrument.
llm_full: A robotic surgical system is provided that includes a robotic arm controlled by a control system and a minimally invasive surgical instrument having an internal U-turn mechanism. The instrument includes a shaft with an end effector and/or wrist mechanism at a distal end, wherein actuating forces are transmitted around at least one U-turn having a bend radius smaller than that of a comparable flexible arm. One or more sensors positioned along the shaft, U-turn mechanism, and/or end effector measure forces, velocities, and tension in tissue during actuation. The control system uses the sensed parameters to modulate both the robotic arm motion and the transmission of actuating forces through the U-turn mechanism to achieve precise manipulation of the distal components while reducing unwanted tissue damage.
llm_title: A surgical instrument is provided that combines controlled jaw closure with retrograde navigation through a bodily lumen or tissue tract. The device includes an elongated shaft bearing a retrograde guidance mechanism and a distal jaw or clamp assembly configured to advance in concert with controlled closure force. A control system coordinates the rate of distal advancement with progressive closure of the jaws to securely capture, manipulate, or occlude target tissue while minimizing trauma. The instrument is particularly suited for procedures requiring access from a distal site toward a proximal target, enabling precise tissue engagement, cutting, or fixation under retrograde advancement conditions.

structure_text: A method for a patient undergoing orthopaedic surgery comprises a device for positioning and adjusting the anatomical portion of a bone implant in a joint. The device may be augmented with a computer-generated guidance system to generate a map of the anatomical portion of a bone implant. In addition, the invention includes methods for obtaining data from a multi-probe imaging system, such as a digital camera, which is used to identify the location of the implant in relation to the anatomical portion of the joint.
llm_full: A system and method for revision orthopedic surgery integrates a hand-held, tracked imaging device with navigation-based implant registration. The system uses real-time radiation imaging from a detector fixed to a radiation source and tracked in six degrees of freedom to acquire intraoperative images of an existing orthopedic implant and surrounding bone and cement. A navigation module registers the patient’s existing implant as a reference structure, fuses the real-time images with preoperative or intraoperative planning data, and generates guidance for controlled removal of bone, bone cement, or prosthetic components. The guidance is provided to navigated, robotic, or articulating hand-held tools, enabling precise, minimally invasive revision and implantation procedures.
llm_title: A surgical planning and navigation system is disclosed that integrates implant-based planning for total joint arthroplasty with a radiographic imaging device. The system includes an imaging apparatus configured to acquire radiographic data of a target joint and implanted fiducial or trial components, and processing circuitry configured to digitize anatomical and implant-related landmarks from the radiographic data. Using these landmarks, the processing circuitry generates a three-dimensional, implant-based surgical plan and registers the patient’s anatomy to the imaging coordinate system in real time. The combined system enables intraoperative adjustment of implant size, position, and orientation based on updated radiographic images to optimize joint alignment and function.

structure_text: 1 The invention comprises a method for establishing a bone satchet relative to the surface of the body of the first osteotomy. The technique is achieved by cutting a portion of a bone satchet into the surface of the body of the first osteotomy. The insertion point of the insertion point is controlled by a coupling tool, which provides a positional adjustment of the insertion point relative to the surface of the body of the first osteotomy. The coupling tool provides a positional adjustment of the insertion point relative to the surface.
llm_full: A system and method for computer-assisted osteotomy planning and execution integrates a virtual haptic environment with a physical fixation plate and bone cutting procedure. A computer generates a virtual model of a bone and associated fixation plate having first and second openings corresponding to first and second voids formed in the bone, and defines first and second subsets of haptic interaction primitives for simulating plate positioning and wedge-opening manipulation in respective haptic subspaces. During a simulated osteotomy, the system determines haptic forces in the first subspace to guide drilling and initial plate fixation, and determines haptic forces in the second subspace to guide relative movement of first and second bone cut surfaces until alignment of the second openings is achieved. The system further outputs real-time haptic feedback to a virtual tool to improve surgical accuracy and stability in translating the planned virtual cuts and plate placement to a physical procedure.
llm_title: A system and method are provided for planning and performing osteotomy procedures with substantially stable haptic feedback. The system generates a three-dimensional surgical plan for bone cutting based on patient-specific anatomical data and simulates the intended osteotomy trajectory. A haptic interface device coupled to the planning and navigation module delivers stable, high-fidelity tactile and force cues to guide the surgeon’s tool along the planned cutting path while compensating for disturbances and hand tremor. The system thereby enhances surgical accuracy, reduces the risk of unintended bone removal, and improves reproducibility of osteotomy outcomes.

structure_text: An imaging system includes a radiation source formed to capture a photon of a radiation source, a handheld device disposed on a fixed surface, and a method of adjusting the position of the handheld device, a handheld device disposed on a fixed surface, and a navigation device disposed on the handheld device.
llm_full: A system for performing implant revision surgery comprises a hand-held imaging device including a radiation source and a detector configured to acquire real-time image data of an implant-bone interface, and a navigation system configured to track a pose of the hand-held imaging device in physical space. A processor is configured to register the real-time image data with a three-dimensional model of the implant and bone, determine information related to an interface area between the implant component and the bone based on the registered data, and generate a planned virtual boundary associated with a portion of the interface area to be removed. A tracked cutting tool is correlated with a virtual tool in the three-dimensional model, and the processor is further configured to impose motion constraints on the cutting tool based on a relationship between the virtual tool and the planned virtual boundary. Removal of the portion of the interface area is guided by the motion constraints to facilitate separation and extraction of the implant component from the bone.
llm_title: A system and method are provided for robotic-assisted surgical revision procedures utilizing integrated radiographic imaging. The system includes a radiographic imaging device configured to generate real-time or near real-time images of a target anatomical region and a robotic manipulator configured to perform revision tasks based on those images. A control unit registers the radiographic images with a pre-operative or intra-operative model and computes updated trajectories, constraints, and tool positions for the robotic system during the revision procedure. The integrated system enables automated or semi-automated guidance, verification, and adjustment of implant placement or hardware removal under continuous radiographic feedback.

structure_text: 1 An orthopaedic surgery device comprising a base unit is configured to generate an image of a patient's position relative to a target joint. The device comprises a control mechanism for adjusting the position of a target joint. The device comprises a control mechanism for adjusting the position of a target joint relative to a target joint. In addition, the invention permits the use of a plurality of optical probes, including a hand-held device and a computer-aided image processing system.
llm_full: A system and method are provided for patient-specific joint repair that integrates handheld intraoperative imaging with customized surgical tools and implants. The system comprises a hand-held radiation-based imaging device with an associated navigation system configured to track its pose relative to a patient’s joint and to acquire real-time image data of a damaged or failed implant and surrounding anatomy. A planning module uses the image data to design or select patient-specific replacement implants and matching surgical instruments, and to generate a surgical plan for partial or total joint arthroplasty or revision. The navigation system further guides the customized tools during the procedure to optimize implant fit, alignment, and functional outcome.
llm_title: A system and method for intraoperative radiographic planning and guidance of revision arthroplasty procedures is disclosed. The system comprises an imaging device configured to obtain real-time radiographic images of a joint region and a set of revision implants and tools configured for removal and replacement of existing joint arthroplasty components. The imaging device and revision tools are operatively integrated such that radiographic data is used to register the position, orientation, and fixation status of the implanted components and surrounding bone, and to guide tool placement, cutting paths, and implant sizing. In certain embodiments, the system provides automated or semi-automated image analysis to generate recommended revision plans and to verify implant positioning during and after the revision procedure.

structure_text: A method of the invention relates to a computer-controlled system for generating a virtual haptic representation of a surgical procedure by using a combination of a simulated haptic model and a predetermined haptic model. The predetermined haptic model is then analyzed for morphological features, such as bone structure and joint surface area. Two methods of the invention are described for generating a virtual haptic representation of a surgical procedure by using a predetermined haptic model and adjusting a predetermined haptic model to a target.
llm_full: A system and method for image-free, haptically guided orthopedic implant revision surgery are disclosed. A 3D model of a target bone is generated from predefined anatomical parameters and iteratively reshaped using surface points collected intraoperatively. A virtual surgical tool is associated with haptic interaction geometric primitives partitioned into a first subset defining stable guidance forces for gross bone preparation and a second subset defining fine correction forces in a different subspace corresponding to localized reshaping. The system computes and renders haptic forces from both subsets to provide substantially stable, multi-resolution tactile feedback while the surgeon modifies the bone to conform to the planned revision model.
llm_title: A system and method are provided for performing image-free revision implant surgery using substantially stable haptics. The system includes a surgical instrument and a haptic interface configured to generate spatially bounded force-feedback fields corresponding to anatomical and implant reference data obtained without intraoperative imaging. A controller computes virtual constraints and safe operating regions based on preexisting implant geometry and intraoperative tracking, and applies haptic guidance forces to the instrument to assist the surgeon in accurately locating, modifying, or replacing the implant. The stable haptic feedback reduces unintended motion and improves precision and safety during revision procedures conducted without real-time imaging.

structure_text: A method for generating and adjusting a computer-based haptic simulation of a surgical intervention system is described. The method consists of determining the articulation of a surgical intervention system with respect to a predetermined articulation of a virtual device. One or more parameters of the virtual device are mapped to a predetermined articulation of a surgical intervention system. The user may use a tool to identify the articulation of a surgical intervention system by referring to a predetermined articulation of a virtual device and adjusting the rotational forces
llm_full: A system and method for robot-assisted orthopedic surgery provides substantially stable, multi-subspace haptic guidance during bone resection. Patient-specific anatomical data is acquired and used to generate a three-dimensional model of a target joint region and to determine a virtual resection volume defining a dynamic movement limit for a cutting tool. A haptic engine identifies first and second subsets of haptic interaction geometric primitives respectively corresponding to gross positioning and fine boundary control of the tool, and computes haptic forces in distinct haptic subspaces to guide tool motion within the virtual resection volume. The robotic system constrains tool movement in real time based on the computed multi-subspace haptic forces, thereby inhibiting motion outside the planned resection while maintaining stable and intuitive surgeon feedback.
llm_title: A computer-assisted surgical system for femoral head reshaping is provided that integrates robotic guidance with substantially stable haptic feedback. The system includes a robotic manipulator configured to position and orient a bone-reshaping tool relative to a patient’s femoral head according to a preoperative plan, and a haptic interface configured to provide the surgeon with stable, bounded force feedback during manual refinement of the tool trajectory. A control module combines real-time imaging or tracking data with the robotic guidance parameters to generate safe virtual boundaries and haptic constraints that resist motion outside a planned resection volume. The integrated system enables precise bone removal while preserving surgeon tactile control and reducing the risk of over-resection or joint surface damage.

structure_text: A surgical imaging system of the present invention includes a method for manipulating an image generated by a surgical instrument to provide a user with a guide to a surgical procedure. A computer-aided image processing tool detects the position of a surgical instrument at a focal point and transmits the image to the surgical instrument. The data generated by the surgical instrument are correlated with the image generated by the surgical instrument. During the operation, an end-to-end visual representation of the image is provided, and multiple images of the image are displayed in three-dimensional space.
llm_full: A system and method are provided for real-time intra-operative 3D navigation that combines Q3D endoscopic imaging with multi-camera IR-based anatomical reconstruction. A patient’s anatomical region is scanned and integrated with reflected IR images from multiple instruments and external cameras to generate a dynamic, parallax-enhanced 3D model of the surgical scene. A processor registers and updates this model with Q3D endoscope data, identifies instruments and critical structures, and determines no-fly zones and predicted instrument paths relative to the reconstructed anatomy. The processor further provides a virtual field of view from any selected instrument or vantage point, enabling continuous 3D tracking and collision-avoidance guidance during surgical procedures.
llm_title: A system and method are provided for enhanced three-dimensional endoscopic imaging that quantitatively visualizes surgical instruments within an augmented-parallax field of view. The system integrates stereoscopic or multi-view endoscopic image acquisition with real-time geometric calibration to determine precise 3D positions and orientations of instruments relative to anatomical structures. An augmented-parallax rendering engine adaptively modifies apparent depth cues and baseline disparities to amplify depth perception while maintaining metric accuracy of instrument localization. The resulting visualization enables improved spatial awareness, collision avoidance, and guidance for minimally invasive procedures.

structure_text: 1 An operating room surgical tool system comprises a camera with a viewfinder, a camera with a viewfinder, a camera with a viewfinder, a camera with a viewfinder, a camera with a viewfinder, a camera with a viewfinder, a camera with a viewfinder, a camera with a viewfinder, a camera with a viewfinder, a camera with a viewfinder, and a camera with a viewfinder. 2 An end-axis position is performed to identify the position of a rotating instrument.
llm_full: A surgical visualization and measurement system for intra-abdominal procedures comprises at least one trocar-mounted retractable camera having a fixed positional relationship with a tracking mark, a laparoscopic or endoscopic wide-field camera, and an optical tracking sensor configured to detect positions of the tracking marks in real time. A processor receives images from the retractable camera and the wide-field camera, determines inter-camera distances and orientations from the tracked marks, and applies image transforms to geometrically register the images. The processor then combines the registered images to generate a stereoscopic three-dimensional representation of tissue structures and to compute accurate three-dimensional shape and distance measurements within the body cavity. The resulting three-dimensional images and measurements are displayed to the surgeon to assist in navigation, manipulation, and planning during minimally invasive surgery.
llm_title: A prospective invention comprises a minimally invasive surgical assistance system integrating a trocar assembly with a stereoscopic image correction and generation module. The trocar includes one or more imaging channels configured to receive image capture devices that acquire distinct monocular images from different viewpoints within a body cavity. A processing unit corrects image data from the distinct images, compensating for optical distortions, misalignment, and tissue-induced artifacts, and generates real-time stereoscopic three-dimensional images of the surgical field. The resulting 3D visual output is provided to a surgeon via a stereoscopic display or head-mounted device, enhancing depth perception and precision during trocar-based procedures.

structure_text: One method relates to a surgical imaging system comprising a manipulating device, an endoscope, and a camera. The manipulating device generates an image of the anatomical position of a patient in a surgical procedure. The imaging system is augmented to provide a virtual image of the anatomical position of a patient in a surgical procedure. In addition, the image is analyzed for accuracy by a data acquisition process. The data acquisition process may be performed remotely from the imaging system, including the acquisition of three-dimensional images of the anatomical position of objects.
llm_full: A system and method for intra-operative three-dimensional imaging and motion-compensated guidance of endoscopic procedures is disclosed. An endoscope equipped with a tracking mechanism is navigated to locations at or near moving target tissue, while cyclical organ motion is captured by motion sensors and correlated with endoscope position and orientation data. Simultaneously, a plurality of IR cameras, mounted on surgical instruments or within the operative field, capture IR images that are associated via parallax to generate an integrated 3D image of the anatomical region in real time. The correlated motion data and integrated 3D image are combined to produce a motion-compensated, real-time intra-operative visualization and navigation map for precise targeting and intervention on moving tissue.
llm_title: A system and method are provided for enhanced endoscopic-guided tumor treatment that integrates tracked bronchoscopy-based motion simulation with augmented parallax endoscopic imaging. A navigation module registers real-time bronchoscope position and orientation with preoperative imaging to model and predict respiratory-induced tumor motion. Simultaneously, an imaging module generates parallax-augmented endoscopic views, providing depth-enhanced visualization of airway and tumor structures. The combined system enables precise, motion-compensated targeting and delivery of diagnostic or therapeutic interventions to tumors within or adjacent to bronchial passages.

structure_text: A surgical instrument system comprises a robotic tool for manipulating a surgically performed joint and a guide device for adjusting the position of the surgically performed joint relative to the patient's body. The method includes a method of generating force to be applied to the surgically performed joint. The method includes a plurality of end-pieces, including a first-axis receptacle and a cutting device. The receptacle is positioned in a pre-determined position relative to the patient's body, and the cutting device is positioned in.
llm_full: A system and method for robot-assisted extraction of orthopedic implants is provided. The system includes a robotic arm having an end effector configured to releasably couple to a pivotable implant extractor tool with jaws adapted to engage an implant. A robotic controller monitors a position and orientation of the end effector and applies controlled forces to the implant via the extractor tool while simultaneously determining soft tissue balance using data from a tracking system. The controller adjusts the extraction trajectory and force based on real-time soft tissue balance feedback, and outputs corresponding information to a display to facilitate atraumatic, single-operator implant removal.
llm_title: A system and method for revision articular surgery integrates real-time soft tissue balancing with an implant extraction tool. The system comprises a sensor-enabled balancing assembly configured to assess ligament tension and joint alignment during removal of an existing implant, and an extractor instrument having adjustable engagement features controlled according to the measured soft tissue parameters. The method includes dynamically modifying extraction force vectors and trajectories to minimize collateral damage to soft tissues and underlying bone while maintaining or improving joint balance. The invention facilitates precise implant removal and preparation for re-implantation while preserving optimal soft tissue tension and joint kinematics.

structure_text: A method is provided for manipulating a portion of a limb to determine the position of a joint relative to the first and second vertebral bones of the limb. The method includes a force sensor and a reversible alignment device. The force sensor is positioned at the proximal end of the limb, and the reversible alignment device is positioned at the distal end of the limb. The reversible alignment device is covered by a flexible plastic covering system comprising a plurality of movable structures, including a bone.
llm_full: A system and method for robot-assisted soft tissue balancing during joint arthroplasty is provided. The system includes a robotic arm having an end effector configured to removably couple to a tensor/ligament balancer including first and second paddles and a biasing member operable to apply a substantially constant force between opposing anatomical surfaces. A robotic controller monitors a position and orientation of the end effector and the tensor/ligament balancer using a tracking system, and determines soft tissue balance based on real-time gap measurements produced by displacement of the second paddle under the constant force. The controller outputs quantitative soft tissue balance metrics and optionally adjusts the applied force and end effector position to achieve a desired balance profile.
llm_title: A system and method for intraoperative soft tissue balancing in articular joint surgery is provided, utilizing a constant-force tensioning apparatus to dynamically assess and adjust ligament balance throughout a range of motion. The invention combines a force-controlled tensor/ligament balancer with real-time measurement of joint gaps, alignment parameters, and soft tissue tension in multiple planes. Using these measurements, the system guides selective soft tissue releases, implant positioning, and component sizing to achieve optimized and reproducible joint kinematics. In certain embodiments, feedback may be provided visually or electronically to the surgeon or a robotic system to automate or semi-automate balancing adjustments.

structure_text: A method comprises a computer-aided robotic system for detecting and mapping the position of a patient during a surgical procedure. The system generates an image of a device based on the information provided by one or more sensors in the system. The system generates an image of a device based on the information provided by one or more sensors in the system. In addition, the system may be configured to display the orientation and orientation of a reference scene from a physical location to a three-dimensional perspective, and to display the orientation and orientation of a reference scene from a virtual location
llm_full: A system and method for robotic-assisted microsurgery integrates a global surgical coordinate framework with intelligent motion classification of surgeon-manipulated controllers. A three-dimensional model of the patient’s anatomy is generated using robotic kinematics and depth-resolved imaging, and a virtual safety boundary is defined within this global coordinate system. One or more freely movable input controllers equipped with inertial sensors provide real-time motion data that is analyzed to distinguish intentional from unintentional surgeon movements. Detected unintentional movements are suppressed or compensated within the coordinate system to prevent tool motion beyond the virtual boundary and thereby reduce the risk of inadvertent tissue injury.
llm_title: A system and method are provided for robot-assisted surgery that integrates a global coordinate framework with user interface motion monitoring. A surgical robot workspace is defined in a unified global coordinate system, within which positions and orientations of surgical instruments are continuously tracked. A user interface device controlling the robot is monitored to detect unintentional or anomalous user movements, such as tremors, slips, or unintended displacements, relative to the global coordinate reference. Upon detection of such unintentional movements, the system automatically modifies, filters, or inhibits corresponding robotic actions to enhance surgical accuracy and patient safety.

structure_text: A surgical apparatus comprises a surgical tool system for generating an image of a surgical instrument and a surgical tool system for manipulating a surgical instrument. The surgical tool system includes a method for determining the relative position of a surgical instrument and a surgical tool system. In addition, the method may be configured to allow a user to rotate the surgical instrument from one end to the other. The method may be configured to allow a user to remove a portion of the surgical instrument from the surgical tool system by means of a first-axis rotation and a third-axis rotation.
llm_full: A robotic-assisted surgical system for ophthalmic procedures includes a global eye-referenced coordinate framework and a deployable, multi-blade retractor assembly. A robotic manipulator positions the retractor assembly relative to a three-dimensional model of the patient’s eye generated from kinematic data and optical coherence tomography images. The first and second retractor blades are rotatably coupled to a clevis and configured such that controlled torque applied to a first blade selectively rotates the second blade in coordination, while maintaining predetermined virtual safety boundaries within the global coordinate system. The system thereby enables precise, image-guided deployment and adjustment of the retractor blades to stabilize ocular tissues while preventing encroachment into protected anatomical regions.
llm_title: A robotic surgical system is provided that utilizes a global coordinate framework to manipulate multi-blade medical instruments within a patient’s body. The system includes a robotic arm assembly, a control unit configured to register patient anatomy and instrument position in a unified coordinate space, and at least one surgical device having multiple blades configured for cutting, grasping, or dissecting tissue. The control unit coordinates the motion and orientation of each blade independently or in concert based on the global coordinate data to achieve precise, repeatable tissue interaction. Methods of use include registering anatomical landmarks, planning multi-blade trajectories, and executing robotically controlled surgical maneuvers under image or sensor guidance.

structure_text: One or more methods of executing a surgical system are described, including the manipulation of a virtual object by a computer-aided robotic device to generate an anatomical image of a surgical scene. The system generates an image of the surgical scene based on the user's perception of the location and orientation of the surgical scene. In addition, the system provides a method for identifying and synchronizing a set of data from a sensor in the operating room to a set of data from a camera in the operating room.
llm_full: A system and method are provided for virtual-reality-based planning, simulation, and execution of robotic-assisted ocular surgery within a unified global coordinate framework. A global coordinate system for a patient’s eye is established using robotic kinematic data and optical coherence tomographic imaging from an overhead optical assembly and a tool-based sensor, thereby generating a computer-registered three-dimensional eye model and associated virtual safety boundaries. A virtual reality environment renders the three-dimensional model and virtual surgical instruments, and receives user inputs to manipulate virtual robotic components corresponding to physical robotic instruments within the established coordinate system. A server-client architecture generates and transmits actuation commands derived from the user inputs and real-time robotic status data, enabling synchronized control and visualization of both the virtual and physical robotic components while enforcing the virtual boundaries to prevent inadvertent injury.
llm_title: A system and method are provided for immersive teleoperated robotic surgery that integrates a global coordinate system with a virtual reality (VR) simulation environment. A robotic surgical apparatus is tracked in a unified global coordinate frame that aligns real-world instrument positions with a corresponding virtual surgical scene presented to a user through a VR display. The system continuously maps and updates the positions and orientations of robotic instruments and patient anatomy in the global coordinate system, enabling accurate, latency-compensated visual and haptic feedback. The combined framework supports pre-operative simulation, intra-operative guidance, and post-operative review by maintaining a consistent spatial relationship between real and virtual surgical environments.

structure_text: A method of the present invention relates to providing an electrically actuated device for a surgical procedure to be implanted in a patient's body. The device includes at least one implantable imaging system, a display device, and an input/output device. The display device and the input/output device are configured to monitor the patient's physiological characteristics, such as sensitivity, temperature, and focal length, by a combination of a signal processing device and a signal processing device.
llm_full: A system and method are provided for visually guided electrical stimulation of tissue during surgical procedures using an optical head mounted display (HMD). The system includes an electrical stimulator having at least one electrode and a power supply configured to deliver capacitive discharge stimulation energy to tissue proximate a target anatomy to induce an observable response. The HMD is configured to receive stimulation parameters and response data and to display, in real time, visual guidance overlays indicative of electrode position, stimulation settings, and tissue responses in the surgeon’s field of view. The integrated system enables precise localization, assessment, and modulation of target anatomical structures during surgery.
llm_title: A system and method are provided for performing minimally invasive surgery with integrated intracorporeal smooth muscle stimulation. The system includes a surgical device configured for access to a target anatomical site and a delivery subsystem adapted to position one or more stimulation electrodes or actuators adjacent smooth muscle tissue. A controller coordinates surgical manipulation with controlled delivery of electrical and/or mechanical stimuli to modulate smooth muscle tone, peristalsis, or sphincter function during the procedure. The invention improves visualization, access, and functional assessment of organs by dynamically adjusting smooth muscle activity in real time while surgery is being performed.

structure_text: This invention relates to a surgical imaging device comprising a method for displaying an image of a patient during a surgical procedure, a technique for manipulating an image of a patient, and an endoscope for guiding the image of a patient to a desired location. In addition, the apparatus may be accessed from a computer-based system comprising a positional camera, a positional camera, a positional camera, a positional camera, a positional camera, a positional camera and a positional camera.
llm_full: A system and method are provided for visually guided, robot-assisted endoscopic surgery using an optical head-mounted display. The system comprises an endoscope configured to provide real-time images of a field of view (FOV) within a body cavity, a maneuvering system defining its own x, y, z axes, and a data processing unit adapted to control the maneuvering system relative to the FOV axes independently of the maneuvering system axes. The head-mounted display presents the endoscopic images and superimposed guidance cues, and receives user inputs corresponding to desired movements of the FOV. The data processing unit translates these user inputs into control signals for the maneuvering system so as to reposition the endoscope in the body cavity according to the FOV-referenced commands while maintaining visual alignment for the surgical procedure.
llm_title: A system and method are provided for integrated surgical control combining robotic surgical devices with a global endoscopic command platform. The invention includes a set of surgical instruments and actuators configured for minimally invasive procedures, operatively coupled to an endoscopic imaging and control unit providing multi-axis visualization and manipulation. A central controller coordinates real-time input from the endoscope, surgeon interfaces, and auxiliary sensors to drive precise instrument positioning, tissue interaction, and safety interlocks. The system enables unified control of imaging, navigation, and operative functions to enhance accuracy, reduce operative time, and facilitate complex endoscopic and laparoscopic surgeries.

structure_text: A method for providing guidance to a user of a virtual anatomical implant device involves generating a virtual anatomical representation of a target anatomical position in relation to a computer-generated haptic parameter. The haptic parameter is mapped to a virtual anatomical representation of a target anatomical position in relation to a computer-generated haptic parameter. One or more of the methods described in the present invention are applied to a virtual anatomical implant device, allowing the user to adjust the positioning of the device and adjusting the orientation.
llm_full: A computer-implemented method for patient-specific haptic guidance of a surgical instrument is provided. The method comprises generating a virtual implant model and a virtual anatomical model of a patient, identifying one or more reference features of the virtual implant model, and determining intersections between the reference features and the anatomical model to define at least one patient-specific haptic boundary. The method further comprises determining, by a processor, a current orientation angle of an axis of a surgical instrument relative to a target axis associated with the reference features, and dynamically adjusting the patient-specific haptic boundary based on the determined orientation angle. The haptic boundary is configured to constrain the instrument from deviating beyond a defined angular and spatial limit while guiding the instrument along a path optimized for the patient-specific anatomy and implant position.
llm_title: A system and method are provided for dynamically generating and adapting haptic guidance boundaries with collapsing geometries for instrument navigation in virtual, augmented, or mixed-reality environments. The system defines customizable interactive haptic boundaries around virtual objects or target paths and couples them to a haptically rendered object that progressively collapses in geometry as the instrument approaches a desired trajectory or endpoint. Real-time sensor data and user interaction parameters are used to modify boundary stiffness, shape, and collapse behavior to provide context-sensitive guidance and error correction. The system thereby enables precise, intuitive control of tools or instruments while reducing cognitive load and improving task performance.

structure_text: A computer-based surgical method is disclosed for obtaining a bone plan for a prosthetic implant in a patient's arthroscopic surgery. The method includes tools for manipulating the articular surface of a prosthetic implant and adjusting the relative positioning of the articular surface of a prosthetic implant. The method also includes a tool system for determining the alignment of the articular surface of a prosthetic implant and adjusting the relative positioning of the articular surface of a prosthetic implant. These components may be used in the preparation of a surgery.
llm_full: A system and method for intraoperatively planning and executing revision arthroplasty using robotic assistance and bone-density-based virtual boundaries. The method includes capturing positions of a tracked probe as it contacts an interface area between bone and an implanted component, and generating, without pre-operative imaging, a first virtual boundary defining material to be removed to detach the component. Bone density data obtained intraoperatively or from limited imaging is further used to generate a second set of virtual objects defining optimal regions for re-implantation, such that distal portions of a revision implant are located in higher-density bone. A robotic guidance station constrains operation of a cutting or machining tool based on both the removal boundary and the density-optimized re-implantation boundaries to facilitate component removal and preparation of bone for revision implantation.
llm_title: A system and method are provided for robotic-assisted revision shoulder arthroplasty utilizing stemless implant components. The system includes a robotic manipulator, imaging and planning software configured to identify and assess previously implanted shoulder components, and tools for atraumatic removal of failed or malpositioned implants. Based on preoperative and intraoperative data, the system generates a revision plan that defines bone resection, preparation, and placement of stemless glenoid and humeral components while accounting for existing bone loss and implant fixation sites. The robotic manipulator then guides execution of the revision plan with real-time feedback to optimize joint alignment, fixation stability, and preservation of remaining bone stock.

structure_text: A method is disclosed for creating bone-based orthopaedic implants for the proximal part of the femur joint. In addition, the method includes a system of repositioning a bone-based orthopaedic implant into the proximal part of the femur joint. The methods are characterized by a first and second scan of the articular surface of the bone and a second and third scan of the articular surface of the bone. In addition, measurements of the articular surface of the bone are used to guide the procedure
llm_full: Systems and methods are provided for patient-specific hip joint arthroplasty that integrate frontal pelvic plane determination with intraoperative kinematic optimization. A pelvic reference frame is established by ascertaining the location of the frontal pelvic plane from x-ray recordings using a pubic point and rear-projection of a straight line through a pelvic contour. Patient-adapted implant components and surgical tools are then aligned and positioned relative to the determined frontal pelvic plane, while intraoperative measurements of joint kinematics are acquired. Implant orientation and sizing are iteratively adjusted in real time based on the pelvic reference and measured kinematics to optimize joint function and stability.
llm_title: A computer-assisted surgical system for hip joint arthroplasty is disclosed, comprising patient-specific implants and cutting guides configured using automatically determined pelvic planes. A pelvic localization device acquires anatomical landmark data and computes functional pelvic reference planes, which are registered to preoperative imaging. Based on the registered pelvic planes, a planning module generates a patient-adapted joint reconstruction plan and associated surgical tools or guides for accurate component positioning. The system thereby enables reproducible alignment of acetabular and femoral components relative to true pelvic orientation, improving fit, biomechanics, and clinical outcomes.

structure_text: The disclosed methods include a device for generating an orthopaedic representation of a patient's body during an arthroplasty procedure. In addition, the disclosed methods include a system for generating an orthopaedic representation of a patient's body during an arthroplasty procedure. In particular, a series of computer-aided devices are incorporated into a device for the purpose of measuring, adjusting, and prioritizing the orientation of two or more articular planes of a patient's body, based on three-dimensional imaging data.
llm_full: Systems and methods are provided for patient-specific joint arthroplasty planning and implant design using 3D body reconstruction from 2D imaging. A consumer-grade 2D camera and motion sensors acquire images of a patient in an unconstrained environment, and automatic segmentation and pose estimation generate a 3D skeletal and soft-tissue model of the relevant joint region. The 3D model is used to derive joint morphology, kinematic parameters, and loading characteristics, which are then employed to design and virtually evaluate patient-adapted implant components and surgical tools. The resulting implant geometries, kinematic simulations, and procedural plans may be shared via networked platforms for remote surgical planning, optimization, and manufacturing.
llm_title: A system and method are provided for patient-specific joint arthroplasty planning and execution using single-image mobile device body scanning and 3D model generation. A mobile device acquires at least one image of a target limb or joint region, from which a calibrated three-dimensional anatomical model is automatically constructed and analyzed to determine joint geometry, alignment, and pathology. Based on the patient-adapted 3D model, customized prosthetic components, cutting guides, and/or surgical tools are virtually designed and output as digital files suitable for fabrication. The system further provides preoperative planning, intraoperative guidance, and postoperative assessment functionalities by integrating mobile-acquired models with patient-adapted arthroplasty workflows.

structure_text: A surgical method relating to the present invention includes a device for displaying a virtual anatomical representation of a patient in the operating room, a surgical tool for determining the anatomical position of a surgical implant, and a surgical tool for determining the anatomical orientation of a surgical implant. One or more data acquisition systems are accessed from a user interface. The data acquisition system is augmented by a guiding lens, which is augmented by a guiding lens, which is augmented by a guiding lens and a guiding lens.
llm_full: A system and method for visually guided hip joint access using an optical head mounted display is disclosed. Pre-operative image data are processed to generate three-dimensional models of the pelvis and femur, which are intra-operatively registered to patient anatomy using tracked probes to form aligned anatomical models and an entry vector cone to a target location. The head mounted display presents, in real time, augmented reality guidance including the aligned models, target location, and entry vector cone overlaid on the patient. A navigated guide wire or instrument is advanced under this visual guidance to achieve accurate and minimally invasive access to the hip joint.
llm_title: A system and method are provided for performing minimally invasive joint surgery that integrates advanced surgical devices with optimized arthroscopic access techniques. The method includes establishing portals to a joint using image-guided or navigation-assisted access procedures, followed by insertion of multifunctional surgical instruments configured for cutting, grasping, tissue resection, and fixation. The devices may include articulating or shape-memory shafts, integrated visualization, fluid management, and energy-delivery elements adapted for use through the established arthroscopic portals. The combined approach enables improved reach, precision, and safety for diagnostic and therapeutic interventions in joints such as the knee, shoulder, hip, and ankle.

structure_text: An apparatus of the invention includes a method for determining a bone alignment relative to a proximal articular joint, a method for generating a bone alignment relative to a distal articular joint, and a method for generating a bone alignment relative to a proximal articular joint. The first and second components of the device, including a loading plate, are inserted into the insertion space to provide a repositioning force to be applied to the insertion space by means of a compression device.
llm_full: A system and method are provided for planning and executing spinal implant procedures using cartilage-based anatomical modeling and mechanically guided distraction. A three-dimensional representation of vertebral bone and associated cartilage regions is generated from measured cartilage points, the regions being defined by control points and projected areas corresponding to candidate implant components. A distractor arm assembly having pivotal segments and a jackscrew-driven collar is registered to the anatomical model and actuated to produce controlled intervertebral distraction and angular adjustment according to a precomputed implant plan. The system displays updated bone and cartilage representations during distraction to guide optimal positioning and selection of spinal implants that accommodate cartilage thickness and spinal instability parameters.
llm_title: A system and method are provided for pre-operative planning and assessment of spinal motion segment units that integrates cartilage-based joint surface modeling with quantitative instability measurement. Imaging data of vertebral bodies and adjacent cartilage or disc-equivalent regions are processed to generate three-dimensional areas representing load-bearing cartilage interfaces within the spine. Motion of the motion segment unit is then measured under controlled loading conditions, and instability metrics are computed by correlating displacement and rotational behavior with the modeled cartilage areas. The combined data are used to plan implant placement, size, and orientation to restore or optimize spinal stability while preserving or mimicking native cartilage contact mechanics.

structure_text: A method of generating a robotic surgical system based on a computer-aided visualization of the patient's anatomy is disclosed. The method includes techniques for adjusting the orthopaedic positioning of a surgical implant in relation to the orthopaedic features of the implant. In addition, a series of tools may be used to obtain a 3-dimensional model of a surgical procedure, such as arthroplasty, arthroplasty, and arthroplasty, to be performed within the patient's own joint space.
llm_full: Systems and methods are disclosed for performing image-free robotic implant revision surgery. A three-dimensional model of a target bone is generated from pre-defined anatomical parameters and iteratively reshaped using surface points acquired intraoperatively. A surgical robotic arm, registered to an external vision system via fiducial markers, positions and orients cutting or drilling tools to execute the revision plan derived from the reshaped 3D model. The robotic arm operates under processor control to guide bone resection and implant placement in real time based on continuous comparison between planned and actual bone geometry.
llm_title: A system and method are provided for performing image-free implant revision surgery using a surgical assistive robotic arm. The system includes a robotic arm configured to hold and manipulate surgical instruments relative to a patient’s anatomy, and a control unit executing image-free planning algorithms to determine optimal implant revision parameters based on intraoperative sensor data and anatomical landmarks. The control unit guides the robotic arm along planned trajectories to prepare bone surfaces, remove failed implants, and position revision implants without reliance on preoperative medical imaging. The system may further provide real-time feedback and adjustment of the robotic arm motion in response to intraoperative measurements to improve implant alignment, fixation, and overall surgical accuracy.

structure_text: A method for actuating a surgical instrument comprises a computer-generated image of a surgical tool and a method for determining the relative position of a surgical instrument at a given surgical location. The method includes a method for generating a first-person feedback signal from a surgical tool and a method for determining the position of a surgical instrument at a given surgical location. In addition, the data collected by the system may be correlated with the data stored in the system, which may be used to calibrate and modify the data stored in the system at various surgical locations.
llm_full: A system and method for task-oriented calibration and control of a robotic surgical device is provided. The method includes calibrating a plurality of objects disposed on an end effector of the robotic surgical device by determining positions and/or orientations of the plurality of objects relative to one another and to a reference location on the device. The method further includes generating a plurality of virtual geometries associated with respective surgical tasks based at least in part on the calibrated positions and/or orientations, tracking a position and/or an orientation of the end effector, and determining whether the end effector is at a location corresponding to a selected virtual geometry. In response to determining that the end effector is at the location corresponding to the selected virtual geometry, the system automatically controls the robotic device to facilitate completion of the surgical task associated with the selected virtual geometry.
