llm_title: A system and method are provided for dynamically guiding user interactions with a haptic device using selectively activatable virtual guide geometries. The invention integrates a haptic control apparatus configured to render variable force feedback with software modules that generate, modify, and activate virtual geometric constraints in response to task context, user input, and environmental data. Virtual guide geometries are selectively engaged to assist the user in performing precise movements, limit motion to safe or optimal paths, and provide context-aware tactile cues. The system further adapts guide activation parameters based on learned user behavior and performance metrics to optimize guidance, comfort, and task efficiency.

structure_text: A device is provided for insertion into the proximal and distal portions of the femur bone and tibia during a knee joint alignment procedure. The device includes a guide for measuring the force exerted on the proximal and distal portions of the femur bone and tibia bone. The guide can be rotated in a fixed position, thereby reducing the stress on the femur bone. An alternative method of adjusting the first and second articulating tips of the guide for insertion into the femur.
llm_full: A system, devices, and methods are provided for dynamically balancing ligament forces during knee replacement surgery using an integrated force-sensing spreader assembly. The system can include a femoral-tibial spreader having opposed forward ends configured to engage the distal femur and proximal tibia, a height-adjustable sensor platform disposed between the forward ends, and multiple force sensors configured to independently measure medial and lateral compartment forces as the spreader is actuated. A radial or digital gauge can display both the distraction distance and the compartmental forces in real time as the handle members are squeezed to tension the ligaments. A method can include inserting the spreader assembly into the joint gap, adjusting both the distraction height and balance between medial and lateral forces, and displaying quantitative force and gap data to guide intraoperative ligament balancing and implant positioning.
llm_title: A computerized knee balancing system is disclosed that integrates a femoral-tibial spreader with real-time tensor measurement for use during knee arthroplasty. The system includes a sensorized spreader assembly configured to be positioned between femoral and tibial bone surfaces, and a control unit that calculates compartmental gap distances, angular alignment, and soft tissue tension throughout a range of flexion. A processor executes algorithms that correlate measured tensor data with predefined balancing parameters and generates guidance signals for intraoperative adjustment of bone resections, implant positioning, and ligament releases. Methods of use are provided for dynamically optimizing knee balance and joint line restoration based on iterative measurements and automated feedback.

structure_text: A device for insertion into the proximal and distal portions of the femur bone (tibia) is provided. The device includes a guide sleeve that can be used to measure the amount of pressure exerted on the proximal and distal portions of the femur bone during arthroscopic surgery. The guide sleeve includes a pivoting mechanism for adjusting the alignment of a joint. A second pivoting mechanism for adjusting the alignment of a joint is provided herein by means of a crossmember.
llm_full: Systems and methods are disclosed for computer-assisted joint replacement incorporating force-sensing distraction during intraoperative alignment. A surgical orientation device and reference sensor establish a three-dimensional axis and cutting plane orientation for a joint, while a ligament-tensioning spreader having an integrated radial force gauge is positioned between opposing bones. Real-time force data from the spreader is correlated with orientation sensor data to dynamically adjust one or more cutting planes and implant positioning to achieve desired soft-tissue balance. The system thereby enables coordinated optimization of bony resection geometry and ligament tension for improved joint kinematics.
llm_title: A system and method for computer-assisted knee joint replacement is disclosed, integrating joint replacement planning with dynamic ligament tension measurement. The system comprises a femoral-tibial spreader having integrated tensor sensors communicatively coupled to a surgical navigation platform that plans and guides implant selection, positioning, and alignment. During trialing and final implantation, the spreader measures compartmental gap distances and ligament tension across flexion ranges, and the system automatically adjusts or recommends implant sizing, positioning, and soft-tissue balancing steps. The combined data-driven workflow improves joint kinematics, reduces instability, and enhances post-operative functional outcomes.

structure_text: A bone alignment device is provided for inserting into the proximal and distal portions of the femur and tibia at the knee joint. The device includes a guide for measuring the pressure exerted by the insertion into the proximal and distal portions of the femur. The guide can be retracted to allow the insertion into the proximal or distal portions of the femur. A second instrument, having a pivotal sleeve, is used to provide a pivotal tool for removing.
llm_full: A surgical knee balancing system is configured to both distract a joint compartment to a predetermined load value and quantitatively measure ligamentous tension during bone preparation for prosthetic implantation. The system includes a femoral-tibial spreader having force-sensing indicia and a moving support structure that pivots relative to a fixed support structure to establish an initial distraction under controlled load. A distraction lock mechanism and an M-L tilt mechanism are selectively engageable to first capture the load-based joint space condition and then forcibly equalize medial and lateral compartments while monitoring changes in measured ligament force. Resultant M-L tilt angles and force measurements are used to guide one or more bone cuts so that the implanted prosthetic component achieves improved alignment and soft-tissue balance.
llm_title: A surgical system for knee arthroplasty is provided that integrates prosthetic component alignment support with dynamic femoral-tibial gap balancing. The system comprises a femoral-tibial spreader having a tensor measurement module configured to quantify joint space tension and ligament balance, and an alignment guide configured to position and orient a prosthetic component with reduced alignment error based on the measured tensor values. A processor is operatively coupled to the tensor measurement module and the alignment guide to calculate optimal implant placement parameters and to provide real-time feedback to the surgeon. The combined functionality enables intraoperative adjustment of both soft-tissue tension and component alignment to achieve a more stable and accurately aligned prosthetic joint.

structure_text: A robotic surgical system comprises a tool for manipulating a surgical instrument and a device for controlling the movement of a surgical instrument relative to a surgical instrument. Methods are provided for identifying the surgical instrument at a first-hand location and the surgical instrument at a second-hand location. One or more actuators may be attached to the surgical instrument to provide an end-to-end transmission of a data path and a data orientation to the surgical instrument. The method of operation described herein may be configured to operate within a specified orientation.
llm_full: A system and method for coordinated control of multiple robotic surgical instruments is provided. A robotic surgical platform manipulates a plurality of surgical tools simultaneously within a patient, while a real-time 3D localization subsystem tracks the spatial positions and movements of each tool. A controller references a movement database and a rules database defining ALLOWED and RESTRICTED movements, including collision prevention, field-of-view, no-fly zones, and tool- and operator-dependent constraints, to dynamically govern each instrument’s motion. The system thereby enables safe, rule-based, and coordinated multi-instrument robotic interventions in real time.
llm_title: A system and method are provided for controlling movement of a robotic surgical system using a rule-based assistance framework for laparoscopic procedures. The system comprises one or more robotic arms configured for minimally invasive access, sensors for capturing intraoperative data, and a controller executing a set of procedural and safety rules derived from laparoscopic surgery best practices. The controller dynamically interprets surgeon inputs, anatomical context, and instrument states to generate constrained motion commands that prevent unsafe trajectories, collisions, or tissue damage. In some embodiments, the system provides real-time guidance, automated subtasks, and context-aware movement limits to enhance precision, consistency, and safety of laparoscopic robotic surgery.

structure_text: A robotic surgical system comprises a method for manipulating a surgical instrument, a surgical tool, and an endoscope. The method may be coupled to an electrically operated surgical instrument, a surgical tool, and an endoscope. The method may be coupled to a patient-centered positioning assister. One or more of the robots in the invention are able to provide control over the movement of a surgical instrument in relation to a corresponding positioning assister, thereby minimizing the need for a surgical tool to be discarded during the procedure.
llm_full: A system and method are provided for coordinated autonomous control of multiple robotic surgical instruments during a medical procedure. A robotic surgical platform supports a plurality of instruments, at least one of which is controlled in supervised autonomy to execute surgical subtasks based on one or more intraoperative imaging modalities. An operating system dynamically plans and updates instrument trajectories to track mobile and deformable targets in an unstructured environment while synchronizing motion among the instruments. The system improves precision, efficiency, and safety by enabling cooperative, image-guided execution of complex multi-instrument surgical workflows.
llm_title: A prospective system provides fully- or semi-automated execution of robotic surgical and interventional procedures using advanced motion control of a robotic surgical platform. The system includes one or more robotic arms, sensors, and a control unit configured to receive preoperative imaging, intraoperative feedback, and surgeon inputs to generate optimized tool trajectories and movement profiles. The control unit dynamically constrains, synchronizes, and adjusts robotic movement in real time to maintain safe clearances, enforce tissue-specific motion parameters, and coordinate multiple instruments during an automated or guided procedure. In some embodiments, the system executes predefined procedural workflows that integrate automated tool positioning, path planning, and intervention steps while allowing surgeon override and fine manipulation through the same motion control framework.

structure_text: A robotic surgical instrument system comprises a plurality of manipulators, including a first-generation manipulator and an endoscope. The manipulators are positioned relative to the endoscope, and a guide mechanism is provided to move the manipulator from one position to the other. An image acquisition device comprising a lattice-transistor motor coupled to a power supply is provided to operate the manipulator. The device is capable of detecting the position of an arm relative to a focal point, thereby minimizing the need for a cutting tool.
llm_full: A robotic surgical system is provided that integrates a precision motion imaging platform with one or more robotically controlled surgical instruments. A high-resolution imaging device is carried on a motion stage under a large-field-coverage lens and is configured to capture both instantaneous telephoto views and wide-angle coverage via temporal integration during a surgical procedure. The robotic controller coordinates instrument motion with dynamic repositioning of the imager to automate tracking of anatomical targets, enhance spatial resolution, and reduce motion blur from either tool or tissue movement. In certain embodiments, multiple coordinated imaging platforms provide depth and range information for improved guidance, without requiring post-processing epipolar rectification.
llm_title: A robotic surgical system is provided that integrates a dynamically positionable imaging assembly for real-time track and range capture of surgical instruments and target anatomy. The system includes a robotic manipulator configured to control movement of one or more surgical tools and a moving imager camera mounted on a controllable support that translates and/or rotates relative to the patient and tools. The controller coordinates motion of the robotic manipulator and the moving imager camera based on intraoperative image data, predicted tool trajectories, and range measurements to maintain an optimal imaging perspective and safe tool path. The integrated control enables continuous, automatic adjustment of both robot kinematics and imaging parameters to improve targeting accuracy, depth perception, and situational awareness during minimally invasive procedures.

structure_text: A portion of the invention relates to a medical imaging device for dissection of the proximal femur. The device includes a trailing guide, a guide lens, and a tool for adjusting the orientation of a trailing guide lens within the body cavity. The device is equipped with a first-in-one orientation adjustment method, which allows the device to be inserted into a patient's body cavity. The device includes a sleeve containing an anchor point and a sleeve containing an anchor point and an anchor.
llm_full: A computer-assisted knee arthroplasty system is provided that integrates a cutting guide apparatus with an optical tracking device for real-time navigation. The cutting guide includes fixed and adjustable cutting blocks having multiple saw slots to perform all required femoral cuts without removal of the guide from the distal femur. The cutting guide further supports an optical tracking head carrying a plurality of light emitters enclosed by dome-shaped lenses of substantially uniform wall thickness to minimize refraction and improve positional accuracy. The system and methods allow precise intraoperative alignment and adjustment of the cutting guide based on tracked spatial data, thereby enhancing implant positioning and surgical outcomes.
llm_title: A prospective invention relates to a computer-assisted knee arthroplasty system employing tracked cutting guides integrated with surgical navigation. The system includes a cutting guide apparatus configured to be fixed to the distal femur and/or proximal tibia and one or more compact tracking devices rigidly mounted to the guide, each tracking device having features manufactured for accurate detection by an optical or electromagnetic navigation system. Real-time positional data from the tracking devices is used to dynamically adjust the orientation and position of the cutting guide relative to patient-specific anatomical landmarks, thereby enhancing accuracy of bone resections. Methods are provided for configuring, calibrating, and using the tracked cutting guide during surgery, as well as for manufacturing the integrated tracking devices to preserve sterility, robustness, and positional precision.

structure_text: This invention comprises a bone anchorage device suitable for the insertion of a first-position guidepiece, a second-position guidepiece, and a third-position guidepiece. The invention comprises a mounting device comprising a disc positioned on the outer surface of the guidepiece. The disc positioned on the outer surface of the guidepiece is disposed on the inner surface of the guidepiece. The disc positioned on the outer surface of the guidepiece is disposed on the inner surface of the guidepiece, and the disc positioned on the inner surface of the guidepiece is removable.
llm_full: A surgical bone marking and resection guidance system is provided, comprising a bone marker device configured to be fixed to a bone segment destined to be resected, and a guidance device removably attachable adjacent to an articular region of the patient. The guidance device includes at least one guiding element with a slot configured to receive a resection instrument and to define a precise cutting plane. The bone marker and/or guidance device further comprise a support having a front and back surface with at least three predetermined openings and a light generating element fixed on the back surface so as to be detectable through the openings by an optical tracking system. The light generating element is reversibly attachable, removable, or replaceable during the operation, thereby enabling real-time tracked positioning and adjustment of the resection guide relative to the bone.
llm_title: A system and method are provided for image-guided surgery integrating an optical tracking marker with intraoperative imaging. The system comprises at least one medical instrument or patient reference outfitted with a marker configured for robust optical detection, the spatial pose of which is continuously tracked by an optical tracking system. The tracked marker position is registered in real time with preoperative and/or intraoperative medical images to update the displayed anatomical overlays and guidance trajectories. This combined approach enables precise localization and manipulation of surgical tools within the patient’s anatomy, improving accuracy and safety of image-guided interventions.

structure_text: This invention provides a method for positioning an implantable device, comprising a first phase assembly comprising a first phase assembly comprising a first phase assembly comprising a first phase assembly comprising a first phase assembly comprising a second phase assembly comprising a second phase assembly comprising a second phase assembly comprising a second phase assembly comprising a second phase assembly comprising a second phase assembly comprising a second phase assembly comprising a second phase assembly comprising a second phase assembly comprising a second phase assembly comprising a second phase clamp.
llm_full: A surgical illumination system is provided that combines a multi-degree-of-freedom intraoperative alignment guide with a hermetically sealed light-emitting module. The alignment guide includes first, second, and third components configured to provide serial adjustment in five degrees of freedom relative to a bone element, while supporting an integrated lamp unit. The lamp unit comprises a light-emitting diode arranged within a hermetically closed housing having a first housing part carrying the diode and a second transparent housing part metallized at least in the solder region and soldered to the first housing part. The integrated system enables precise positioning of the illumination source in three-dimensional space in coordination with implant alignment, thereby improving visibility and accuracy during surgery.
llm_title: A computer-assisted surgical illumination system is provided for preparing a bone element for an implant. The system comprises alignment guides configured to interface with a navigation or robotic platform and to define precise cutting or drilling planes, and at least one LED lamp arranged in a hermetically sealed housing. The hermetically sealed LED lamp is integrated with or attachable to the alignment guides to provide sterilizable, shadow-minimized, and directionally controlled illumination of the surgical field in correspondence with the guided alignment axes. The system thereby improves accuracy and visibility during orthopedic procedures while maintaining sterility and durability of the illumination components.

structure_text: A surgical method for gauging the proximal portion of a femoral skeleton is incorporated. A laser beam is deposited onto the proximal femoral skeleton to generate a first-and second-generation photoreceptors that can be used to adjust the orientation of the femoral skeleton. The system includes a surgical tool for insertion of the implant and a conductive adhesive tape. The conductive adhesive tape is positioned in a fixed position relative to the conductive surface of the implant.
llm_full: A computer-assisted revision knee arthroplasty system is disclosed in which a revision femoral component having thicker distal and posterior bearing portions is implanted to restore the natural anatomic transverse joint plane and collateral ligament balance, while being guided by an optical surgical marking system. The system employs at least three marking heads with light spot lamps projecting visible and non-visible wavelength markers onto the distal femur and associated cutting jigs, and a light spot detection system linked to a computer display for real-time alignment and control. The marking heads are used to define and track reference planes for resection and component positioning, thereby improving accuracy in preparing the distal femur for the revision femoral component. The invention further provides software algorithms that integrate optical tracking data with predefined anatomical targets to optimize implant alignment in both extension and flexion.
llm_title: A computer-assisted system and method for revision knee arthroplasty integrates prosthesis removal instrumentation with an optical surgical marking and alignment subsystem. The system comprises knee prosthesis extraction tools configured to interface with existing implant geometries and at least three light-emitting marking elements affixed to bone-referenced guides or instrument surfaces. A light spot detection unit captures and processes the positions of the marking elements in real time to determine anatomical axes and desired implant orientation. The combined system enables precise removal of a failed knee prosthesis and accurate alignment and placement of a replacement prosthesis based on intraoperative optical tracking.

structure_text: A surgical instrument system comprises a method for determining the orientation of a surgical tool relative to a patient's femoral bone and a method for generating and removing surgical guidepieces. The surgical tool comprises a series of electrodes that are positioned on a surgical surface to be surgically cut. The first electrode is equipped with a photosensitive coating to provide a visible light source. The second electrode is positioned at a pre-determined position relative to the surgical guidepiece and is not subjected to a pressure adjustment during the procedure.
llm_full: A patient-specific surgical instrument system is provided that integrates adjustable cutting guides with an optical marking and alignment subsystem. The instrument includes a bone-conforming attachment body derived from patient imaging data, at least one adjustable cutting guide for arthroplasty procedures, and a plurality of marking heads configured to project light spots in visible and/or non-visible wavelengths onto the bone and guide surfaces. A light spot detection system coupled to a computer display tracks the projected marks in real time to verify and adjust the position and orientation of the cutting guide relative to the patient-specific anatomy. The system enables intraoperative soft tissue balancing and precise alignment of bone resections through combined mechanical adjustment and optical feedback.
llm_title: A computer-assisted surgical system is disclosed comprising a handheld surgical instrument and an integrated optical marking and alignment subsystem. The instrument includes at least one operative end-effector (e.g., cutting, drilling, or suturing element) and a handle configured to receive positional guidance. The marking subsystem comprises at least three marking elements each fitted with a light spot lamp and a light spot detection system arranged to generate and track light spots on the patient’s anatomy or reference surfaces. The detected light spot positions are processed to determine the spatial orientation of the instrument in real time and to guide or constrain the instrument’s operative movements relative to a planned surgical trajectory or target region.

structure_text: An alignment device comprises a proximal section of a femoral cross-section, a guide tube extending from the proximal end of the femoral cross-section, and a receptacle extending from the proximal end of the femoral cross-section. The guide tube is inserted into the proximal end of the femoral cross-section to provide a free-standing mounting point for the insertion of a cutting tool. A second mounting point (1) is provided to provide a fixed base.
llm_full: A surgical navigation system for unicompartmental knee replacement comprises femoral and tibial intramedullary rods carrying adjustable cutting blocks as described for unicompartmental resurfacing, in combination with one or more removable light-generating marker assemblies fixed to the cutting blocks and associated instruments. Each marker assembly includes a support having at least three openings at predetermined positions and a light-generating element fixed to the back of the support so that light is detectable through the openings by an optical tracking system. During surgery, the markers are placed, removed, or replaced on the cutting guides and templates without disturbing their mechanical fixation to bone, thereby enabling real-time tracking and recalibration of the bone preparation and implant positioning steps. The system thus provides computer-assisted, optically tracked guidance for precise alignment, orientation, and depth control of femoral and tibial cuts in unicompartmental knee arthroplasty.
llm_title: A computer-assisted surgical system and method for unicompartmental total knee arthroplasty is provided, wherein patient-specific bone preparation and implant positioning are guided by an optical tracking subsystem employing specialized markers. The knee arthroplasty instrumentation, including cutting guides and alignment jigs, is configured with integrated optical markers adapted for robust detection and pose estimation by an external optical tracking system. Real-time positional data from the markers are used to register the patient’s anatomy, track instrument movement, and compute optimal implant alignment parameters. The system enhances surgical accuracy by continuously updating the planned bone resection and implant orientation based on the spatial relationship between the tracked instruments and the patient’s unicompartmental knee anatomy.

structure_text: A surgical instrument system comprises a detector and a surgical cutting tool. The detector is positioned relative to a surgical eye and a surgical guide is positioned relative to a surgical eye. The surgical guide is positioned relative to a surgical eye and a surgical guide is positioned relative to a surgical eye. One end of the detector comprises a first-order rotational position adjustment mechanism for generating an electrical signal at least 20 nm from a beam of light. The rotational position adjustment mechanism allows the insertion of a second-order rotational position adjustment mechanism.
llm_full: A computer-assisted distal femoral cutting system integrates a valgus-adjustable intramedullary cutting block with a multi-head optical marking and alignment subsystem. The cutting block includes a tubular sleeve for receiving an intramedullary rod and a threaded locking mechanism for fixing valgus orientation, as in a conventional distal femoral cutting guide. A plurality of marking heads with light emitters, operable across visible and non-visible wavelengths, are mounted on or referenced to the cutting block to project positional light spots onto the bone or reference surfaces. A light spot detection system linked to a computer display tracks the projected marks in real time and provides feedback to the surgeon for precise alignment and locking of the cutting block in the desired orientation.
llm_title: A computer-assisted distal femoral resection system is provided for use in knee joint replacement surgery, combining a mechanical cutting guide with an optical surgical marking and alignment subsystem. The cutting guide is configured to be fixed to the distal femur and to define one or more cutting planes for resecting the bone. A plurality of marking elements, each including a light spot lamp and a corresponding light spot detection unit, are arranged on or in association with the cutting guide to project and detect light patterns that indicate positional and angular alignment relative to preselected anatomical or prosthetic reference axes. The integrated system enables real-time visual and/or electronic feedback to accurately orient the cutting guide prior to and during bone resection, thereby improving precision and reproducibility of the distal femoral cut.

structure_text: An embodiment of the invention relates to a surgical instrument suitable for insertion into a pelvic joint. The instrument includes a first method of cutting the instrument, a second method of cutting the instrument, and a second method of adjusting the instrument. The instrument includes a guide shaft, which is positioned at the distal end of the instrument, and a fillet, which is positioned at the proximal end of the instrument. The fillet is provided with a flexible insulating material (including a conductive material) to provide a flexible surface.
llm_full: A patient-specific surgical instrument system is provided for orthopaedic arthroplasty, comprising a bone-conforming body with an attachment area configured from patient imaging data for unique positioning on a patient’s bone, and at least one adjustable cutting guide. The instrument further comprises an integrated illumination module including a hermetically sealed housing with a light-emitting diode, wherein a first housing part bearing the diode is soldered to a second, transparent housing part having a metallized soldering region. The illumination module is positioned to project light through the transparent housing to delineate cutting planes and/or soft-tissue balancing reference zones on the bone during surgery. An adjustment mechanism is operable to change both the position of the cutting guide and the orientation and/or focus area of the illumination to provide real-time visual guidance.
llm_title: A surgical illumination system is disclosed, comprising a hand-held surgical instrument and an integrated LED light source arranged in a hermetically sealed housing. The hermetically sealed LED module is disposed at or near the distal end of the instrument to provide localized, shadow-free illumination of a surgical field while protecting the LED and associated electronics from bodily fluids and sterilization media. The housing is configured to withstand repeated sterilization cycles without loss of sealing integrity and to dissipate heat generated by the LED. In some embodiments, the system further comprises control circuitry for adjusting light intensity and/or color temperature to optimize intraoperative visibility.

structure_text: A medical imaging system of disclosed embodiments includes a device configured to generate an image based on a synchronized motion of a first-person viewfinder and a second-person viewfinder. At least one of the first-person viewfinders is configured to transmit the image to a manipulator. The manipulator is configured to receive signals from a plurality of manipulators. The manipulators are configured to provide a control mechanism for determining the orientation, intensity, and direction of the image at a given point in the system.
llm_full: Systems and methods are disclosed for mediated-reality control of medical instruments using light-field imaging. Light-field data of an anatomical site is captured by an imaging assembly and used to render one or more virtual cameras corresponding to a first medical instrument and a second medical instrument accessing the anatomical site via different access paths. A head-mounted display presents images from the virtual cameras to a user together with a visual representation of the instruments and their relative orientations. Directional input signals received from an input device are interpreted in view of the virtual camera viewpoints to control movement of at least the second instrument relative to the first instrument in three-dimensional space.
llm_title: A system and method are provided for a mixed-reality medical instrument driving platform that integrates light field capture and rendering within a head-mounted display. The system tracks and controls one or more medical instruments while generating a real-time volumetric light field representation of the operative field, including both patient anatomy and instrument position. The head-mounted display renders perspective-correct, depth-accurate views to the operator, enabling precise manipulation of instruments based on immersive visual feedback. The platform further supports remote or semi-autonomous instrument driving by transmitting light field and control data between local and remote operators or robotic subsystems.

structure_text: The present invention provides a method for performing at least one surgical procedure involving a robotically aligned surgical apparatus. The method includes a method for inserting a surgical apparatus into a patient's body cavity, and a method for extracting bone fragments from the surgical apparatus. The surgical apparatus comprises a plurality of components, each of which is supported by a semi-permanent screw system. The components of the surgical apparatus are configured to be coupled to a self-assembly and/or self-assembly elements.
llm_full: A system and method for robot-assisted surgical implantation using image-based physiological region analysis is disclosed. The method comprises acquiring a color medical image of a surgical site, calculating at least one pixel color feature (PCF) value for each pixel, and filtering the PCF data with at least one spatial adaptive bandpass filter (ABPF) to segment physiologically significant regions relevant to implant placement. A robotic system having one or more coordinated arms uses the segmented physiological regions to plan trajectories and synchronously insert multiple screws, rods, or implant components while monitoring insertion progress relative to the identified regions. The insertion is completed autonomously or semi-autonomously with dynamic adjustment of robotic motion based on updated image-derived PCF and ABPF outputs.
llm_title: A system and method for computer-assisted surgical implant planning and placement are disclosed. Medical image data of a patient is processed to generate a three-dimensional anatomical model with segmented regions corresponding to target implantation sites and critical structures. Based on the model, an optimal implant configuration and trajectory are computed, and placement instructions are synchronized with intraoperative tracking of surgical instruments and implant hardware. The system provides real-time guidance to ensure accurate, anatomically conforming, and coordinated placement of multiple implant components.

structure_text: An embodiment of the present invention includes a robotic surgical system for performing a variety of surgical procedures. The robotic surgical system comprises a robot-operated device, a robot-operated device, and a robot-operated device. The robot-operated device is connected to at least one end member of the surgical apparatus. The robot-operated device is shown to facilitate insertion of sutures into the surgical apparatus, and the robot-operated device is connected to the surgical apparatus by means of a movable axis, and the robot-operated device is connected to.
llm_full: A robotic surgical system is provided for autonomously placing and securing multiple surgical implant components using image-derived non-visible property information. The system comprises a console, multiple coordinated robotic arms carrying implant insertion instruments, and at least one imaging instrument configured to capture images of a region of interest during implant insertion. A controller processes the images with one or more filters to identify non-visible properties of anatomical structures and implanted components, such as tissue density, stress distribution, or implant-bone engagement. Based on the identified properties, the controller synchronizes and dynamically adjusts the insertion trajectories and forces of the multiple robotic arms, and completes the implant placement autonomously or in cooperation with a surgeon.
llm_title: A system and method are provided for augmented-reality-guided placement of surgical implant hardware using a robotic surgical platform. The system integrates preoperative and intraoperative imaging to generate an augmented surgical scene that overlays virtual models of implants, trajectories, and anatomical landmarks in real time. A robotic manipulator is controlled to position and insert implant hardware along synchronized, system-calculated paths while the augmented reality environment updates based on tool tracking and tissue deformation. The system further enables automated or semi-automated adjustment of implant orientation and depth based on intraoperative feedback to achieve optimal placement accuracy and alignment.

structure_text: The invention provides a surgical technique for manipulating a portion of the body to be surgically implanted into a region of the body to be surgically implanted. A plurality of endoscopes are positioned at least perpendicular to the insertion device. The plurality of endoscopes are positioned at least perpendicular to the insertion device. In this embodiment, a resonant laser beam is generated from the insertion device, and the resonant laser beam is transmitted to the insertion device.
llm_full: A robotic minimally invasive surgical system integrates multi-arm implant insertion with fluorescence-guided imaging. An illuminator provides intermittent visible color components and fluorescence excitation light to a surgical site while an image capture system acquires corresponding visible images and fluorescence images. A controller generates and displays a real-time background grayscale image of the surgical field with superimposed, color-highlighted fluorescence regions indicating target tissue or critical anatomical structures. The robotic arms autonomously or semi-autonomously coordinate synchronous insertion of screws, rods, or other implant components based on the fluorescence-guided visualization and monitored insertion progress.
llm_title: A surgical navigation system is disclosed that integrates fluorescence-based background imaging with synchronized placement of implant hardware. The system employs selective spectral illumination to generate enhanced-background surgical images in which anatomical structures and critical tissues are distinguished via fluorescence contrast. Real-time tracking and coordination of implant instruments and hardware are synchronized with the fluorescence-guided display, enabling precise alignment and placement relative to highlighted anatomical landmarks. The method improves accuracy and safety of implant procedures by dynamically adjusting implant positioning based on continuously updated fluorescence-enhanced visual feedback.
